title: POC Weekly Lab Readout - Silverstrand bench results & baseline contrast
summary: Weekly POC sync to review lab benchmark results comparing Redwood POC to Silverstrand's baseline provider. Covered latency (p50/p95), throughput (tokens/sec and rps), batching/quantization tradeoffs, routing/fallback behavior, and security/compliance questions. Agreed next steps: 12h sustained load run, share security pack, pricing + dedicated slot proposal, and scheduling legal review next week.
meeting_header: Date: 2026-11-13 | Start: 14:00 PST | End: 14:54 PST | Duration: 54m | Location: Zoom | Recording available | Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez (Redwood) — Raj Patel, Elena Morales, Harrison Wu (Silverstrand)
transcript: [00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we got about 54 minutes, just to run through the lab numbers we promised and find alignment on the next steps.
[00:12] Raj: Yep thanks Maya, excited to see the results. We've been running your harness side-by-side with our baseline this week.
[00:20] Diego: Great — quick agenda review: latency + throughput contrasts, a couple anomaly spikes we saw at high concurrencies, tuning notes (quantize + batch), and then ops/security Qs.

[00:35] Elena: Quick context — baseline is LegacyVendorX using FP16 on A100s, default batching, no prefix caching. Our production SLA is 250ms p95 for 128-token prompts, and cost target is 40% lower than current.

[01:05] Maya: Perfect. First slide — p50/p95 numbers. Redwood POC (opt-quant profile) p50 is 58ms, p95 190ms at 128 tokens; baseline p50 72ms, p95 230ms. So our median is noticeably lower and tail is improved but still some room.
[01:40] Harrison: Wait, are those end-to-end numbers including network egress? Or just inference time on the GPU?
[01:48] Diego: Those are end-to-end from the harness — so include network hop inside the VPC we set up. For pure kernel time avg we're ~40ms p50.
[02:05] Raj: The p95 190ms is interesting — baseline had a few 600ms outliers earlier this week. What caused those?

[02:18] Diego: We saw KV cache misses in the early prefix-window for some scenarios, and a couple of cold-starts on dedicated slot scaling events. We added pre-warm policy which removed the big tail; the 190ms is after the pre-warm change.
[02:45] Elena: Can you explain the KV cache misses — we're not entirely sure how that interacts with our prompt shapes.

[02:52] Diego: Sure. When you have many unique prefixes the KV cache hit rate drops; that increases token compute because you can't reuse KV. We recommended grouping similar requests by routing key and enabling prefix caching — that's in the config we pushed to the lab harness.
[03:10] Raj: Makes sense. How about throughput? We ran a ramp to 1200 rps, what's the tokens/sec you saw?

[03:18] Maya: At 1200 rps with 64-token average prompt, Redwood sustained ~76k tokens/sec across the pool with 95% availability. Baseline sustained ~58k tokens/sec and we saw increased error rates when they hit 85k tokens/sec.
[03:36] Harrison: Those error rates on baseline were timeouts or rate-limited?
[03:40] Elena: Mostly timeouts — they hit queueing in the vendor's front-end, we captured traces.
[03:46] Diego: On Redwood we can shard by model variant and route lower-priority traffic to a quantized variant to keep latency SLOs intact — we demonstrated that in sprint 2.
[04:02] Raj: Can you quantify the quality delta when you use quantized flavor? Our NLU accuracy matters for downstream intent classification.

[04:09] Diego: Absolutely we ran an eval on your dev set: float16 baseline accuracy 92.4%, Redwood quantized int8-perf accuracy 91.8% — a 0.6% absolute drop. For the majority of low-risk paths we recommend the quantized variant; for mission-critical routes you can pin to a higher-precision variant.
[04:34] Elena: 0.6% is acceptable on many flows, but we need to flag a couple of regression prompts. Can you provide per-prompt diffs?
[04:42] Maya: We'll attach the diff report from the eval — Diego will own collecting the failed cases and sending them over.
[04:50] Raj: On cost, the lab numbers suggest 32% lower per-token cost projected if we use Redwood's routing + caching. Is that accurate?

[04:58] Maya: From the harness economics modeled, yes — caching reduced repetitive token compute and smart batching during peaks kept effective GPU utilization higher, lowering unit cost to roughly -32% vs baseline for your traffic shape.
[05:15] Harrison: Can you explain batching strategy? We worry about increased p95 if you batch too aggressively.

[05:20] Diego: We use dynamic batching with a latency cap — by default we set 15ms wait for a batch or max batch size of 64 tokens. That keeps median benefits while limiting the tail. For spikes we fall back to a low-latency path.
[05:34] Elena: Any odd failures during the runs? I saw a note about some adapter misconfig at 02:00AM in the log.

[05:40] Diego: Yes, there was a config drift on one of the worker pools where kernel selection didn't pick the quantized kernel — caused a transient 3x latency blip. We pushed a config lock and that hasn't reappeared.
[06:00] Raj: Security/compliance — we need SOC 2 Type II attestation and KMS integration. Where are we on those docs?

[06:07] Maya: We have SOC 2 in our security pack (PDF) and KMS integrations for both customer-managed keys and Redwood KMS. We'll share the pack after this call. Diego, correct me if I'm wrong on audit log retention options.

[06:20] Diego: Right — audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM, we support 90/365/730-day retention options. We also offer exportable TLS-terminated traces and request-level metadata for compliance reviews.
[06:35] Harrison: Do you support on-prem or VPC private deployments? We need to run in our VPC for PHI workloads.
[06:41] Maya: Yes — Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packages. For the pilot we ran a customer-managed VPC overlay; for PHI you can choose Private with HSM-backed KMS.
[06:52] Raj: Good, legal will want E2E encryption + key separation. We'll loop them in next week.
[07:00] Elena: Back to benchmarks — can you show the latency distribution graph you mentioned?

[07:06] Diego: (screen share) Here's p50/p75/p95/p99 over the 12-hour run. Notice the small plateau around 30 minutes during the artificial traffic burst — baseline had a larger plateau and a big tail spike at p99.
[07:26] Raj: Ok seeing that now. There's a little wobble at 2h30m on Redwood — what's the root cause?
[07:33] Diego: That was autoscaler oscillation caused by a transient network noise in the test harness. We're tuning the autoscaler hysteresis to avoid that.
[07:45] Maya: On the routing side we used policy: latency-first for critical routes, cost-first for batch jobs. That dropped average cost without hurting your critical p95.
[07:55] Harrison: How deterministic are the numbers? We care about reproducibility so our procurement can sign off.

[08:00] Diego: We commit to a reproducible harness: same seed data, same concurrency patterns, same warm-up. We'll hand you the harness repo and exact environment variables so you can run it in your lab.
[08:12] Elena: Can we run a 12h sustained load with a mixed prompt distribution including long-tail prefixes? That was our main concern.
[08:20] Maya: Yes, we'll schedule that — propose to run it Thursday 11/18 starting 0200 UTC to avoid regional contention.
[08:28] Raj: OK. Also need a lane for legal to review security docs — can you set up a separate meeting?
[08:34] Maya: I'll send invites for a legal + security review on 11/19. We'll include our compliance lead and solutions engineer.
[08:40] Harrison: There was one note in the harness about fallback behavior — when a model variant is overloaded does the system fall back to another model or queue?

[08:48] Diego: We implement graceful fallback: route to compatible model variant (e.g., a slightly smaller one) or a quantized fallback. We avoid queueing where it would break SLOs and use a degrade-first pattern.
[08:58] Elena: Good. For observability — can we get token-level traces and per-token cost breakdowns? Procurement asked for that for chargeback.
[09:05] Maya: Yes — per-route token breakdown and per-request cost are available via Redwood Console export/CSV.
[09:10] Raj: About dedicated capacity — is there a minimum commitment?

[09:14] Maya: Dedicated pools start at 4x A100-equivalent slots for enterprise pilots, but we can do a smaller carve for the lab under a time-limited pilot agreement. We'll include a pricing tier in the proposal.
[09:26] Harrison: What's the rollback story if we see regressions after rollout?
[09:30] Diego: We provide canary rollouts, automatic fallback policies and immediate routing back to baseline model if delta passes thresholds. You can also pin traffic percentages per route.
[09:42] Elena: Any notable anomalies in quality across the eval set?
[09:46] Diego: Two prompt families showed repeatable hallucination differences — we logged and will include the per-prompt diffs. They're edge-cases but worth reviewing.
[09:58] Raj: Okay, let's capture action items and owners now.

[10:02] Maya: I'll read them out. Action items: (1) Diego — provide per-prompt diff report and failed-cases by EOD 11/14; (2) Maya — send security pack and pricing + dedicated slot proposal by 11/17; (3) Redwood infra — schedule 12h sustained run 11/18 and deliver raw harness logs; (4) Raj/legal — confirm attendees for 11/19 security review. Any changes?
[10:34] Raj: That looks right. Add one: Harrison will provide the production prompt distribution sample by 11/15 so you can seed the long-tail test.
[10:43] Maya: Added. We'll also put a shared spreadsheet with timeline and gating criteria: cost delta >= 25% and p95 <= 250ms as initial success criteria.
[10:55] Elena: Quick question — for the 12h run do you need a dedicated slot or can it run on the shared pilot pool?
[11:01] Diego: Prefer dedicated ephemeral slot to avoid noisy neighbors; we'll allocate from Redwood Dedicated for the test window.
[11:08] Raj: Any final outstanding technical concerns from your side?
[11:11] Harrison: We'll want to validate KMS integration in a staging KMS before production key handover. Also want to test audit log export to Splunk.
[11:20] Maya: Noted — we'll coordinate with your SRE and security team on the Splunk connector and key rotation test.
[11:27] Elena: Timeline check — if the 12h run is clean and legal signs off, what's the earliest we can move to a limited production carve?
[11:36] Diego: Assuming positive results and legal/compliance sign-off, we can do a soft carve within 2 weeks — provisioning and proving the dedicated pool typically takes 5-7 business days.
[11:48] Raj: Good. Any competitor callouts we should be aware of?
[11:52] Maya: You mentioned LegacyVendorX; others sometimes bring up Anthropic and Vertex. We compared available latency publicly and our internal runs are favorable for this workload.
[11:59] Elena: Ok, thanks. Let's recap next steps and owners one more time.

[12:05] Maya: Recap: Diego — per-prompt diffs by 11/14; Harrison — share prod prompt sample by 11/15; Maya — security pack + pricing by 11/17; Redwood infra — 12h run 11/18 and deliver logs; legal review meeting scheduled 11/19. We'll re-sync after the 12h run for results triage.
[12:30] Raj: Sounds good, appreciate the level of detail. We'll be watching the diffs closely.
[12:36] Maya: Thanks everyone. I'll follow up with calendar invites and upload the harness and logs to the shared drive.
[12:45] Elena: Endorse. Bye all.
[12:48] (call ends)

[53:00] Note: timestamps above reflect the start of topics; full recording available in Zoom for precise offsets. Transcription contains some mis-hears (K-B cache for KV cache in one chunk, Redwood Dedicate instead of Redwood Dedicated in another).
